description:
About the Fellowship

The Royal Society University Research Fellowship is a highly competitive, fully funded fellowship that supports outstanding early-career scientists to become independent researchers. It is ideal for AI/CS researchers who want to build their own research group in the UK.

Funding & Benefits

  • Salary: Full salary (typically £45,000-£60,000 per year)
  • Research Expenses: £90,000 per year for research costs, equipment, and travel
  • Duration: 5 years (initially 3 years, renewable for 2 more)
  • Location: Any UK university or research institution
  • Additional Benefits: Mentoring from a Royal Society Fellow, access to exclusive networks

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Career Stage: Early-career researchers (typically within 3-5 years of PhD completion)
  • Nationality: Open to UK and international applicants
  • Research Area: Natural sciences, including AI, computer science, and interdisciplinary research
  • Track Record: Exceptional research potential with publications in top-tier venues

Application Process

  1. Identify host institution and sponsor.
  2. Develop research vision (5-page outline of long-term research goals).
  3. Submit application to Royal Society.
  4. Review and interview process.
  5. Award notification.

Required Documents

  • Research Vision (5-page outline)
  • CV highlighting significant achievements and publications
  • Sponsor Letter from a senior scientist at host institution
  • Head of Department Statement confirming institutional support

Timeline & Deadlines

Official Link

https://royalsociety.org

Important Notes

  • The Royal Society is the UK's national academy of sciences.
  • Emphasize how your AI research addresses fundamental scientific questions or has potential for significant societal impact.
  • 5 years of funding allows building a substantial research program.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: September 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
